newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Britons detained for carrying cocaine in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Britons detained for carrying cocaine in Venezuela.

text.p: Two British tourists detained when airport customs officials said they found 22 pounds (10 kg) of cocaine strapped to their chests could be charged with international drug trafficking, Venezuelan authorities said on Friday.

James Miles, 18, and Paul Clark, 20, from Leicester in England, were bound for London on a VIASA flight after a 10-day stay in Venezuela when they were stopped on Monday at Maiquetia International Airport's customs, the Anti-Drug Enforcement Agency said. Officials allege each had about 11 pounds (5 kilos) of cocaine packed under his shirt.

Miles and Clark, who said they had been vacationing in Venezuela, said they were forced to carry the drugs after a man put a gun to their heads near a gate of the airport terminal. They gave statements to the Venezuelan public prosecutor on Thursday.
The prosecutor is considering the statements and will decide whether to bring charges by Tuesday, when the two men are due to appear in court.

"We're innocent, we haven't done anything," Miles said on Wednesday night. "A man put a pistol against our heads, he was going to shoot us and told us to go through the airport, through customs ... He watched us do it all."

The men told Reuters they had approached airport customs to tell them about the drugs they had been forced to carry but a misunderstanding arose due to the language barrier. But a National Guard spokesman rejected the Britons' version.
Miles and Clark were being held by the National Guard in Caracas. British embassy officials said on Friday they were being correctly treated by the authorities.
